title: Trump Threatens Harvard's Tax-Exempt Status Via Truth Social Post
description_short: Trump Threatens Harvard's Tax-Exempt Status Via Truth Social Post
description_medium: On May 2, 2025, President Trump posted on Truth Social that his administration would revoke Harvard University's tax-exempt status, writing 'We are going to be taking away Harvard's Tax Exempt Status. It's what they deserve!' Federal law explicitly criminalizes executive branch officials requesting IRS audits of specific entities. Harvard's president called the threatened action 'highly illegal' and 'destructive.' The IRS had begun internal planning for the revocation. The threat escalated the administration's campaign against Harvard, which had already seen over $2.7 billion in funding frozen or cut.
description_long: On May 2, 2025, President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that his administration would take away Harvard University’s tax-exempt status, adding that the university deserved it. The post came amid the administration’s dispute with Harvard over its policies and federal funding. Harvard’s president called the threatened revocation highly illegal and destructive. NBC News reported that tax and legal experts said the post could complicate an effort to revoke Harvard’s status: the IRS has authority to change an organization’s tax treatment, but the president may not direct the agency to investigate a particular taxpayer. Experts said the public threat could support an argument that any action was politically motivated. The post was a threat, not a completed revocation; NBC’s report describes no change to Harvard’s status. The episode raised concerns about pressure on the IRS to act against a named institution and about the agency’s independence.

title: NIH Cancels $800M+ in LGBTQ Health Research Grants
description_short: NIH Cancels $800M+ in LGBTQ Health Research Grants
description_medium: An April 2025 NBC News report says NIH canceled more than 270 LGBTQ-health research grants involving at least $125 million in unspent funds. Researchers expected the total to be higher, but the article does not support the $800 million figure in the existing title. The affected work included HIV and STI prevention, cancer, youth suicide and mental-health research.
description_long: Between January and May 2025, NIH canceled more than 270 grants for LGBTQ-related health research, according to the linked NBC News account. The report puts the documented amount at at least $125 million in unspent funding; researchers told NBC they expected the total to be higher, but that does not establish the $800 million figure in the existing title. The affected work included HIV and STI prevention, cancer, youth suicide, mental health and studies of health disparities among gay and transgender people. Cancellation letters generally said projects no longer fit NIH priorities; some cited executive orders about transgender identities or diversity, equity and inclusion. Researchers described disruptions to continuing studies and possible job losses. One project leader said about half of a 120-person team relied on the canceled awards. The article also described related HHS layoffs affecting CDC HIV surveillance among gay men and a lab testing drug resistance in bacteria that cause sexually transmitted infections. NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya said the agency would move away from research it considered focused on DEI or gender identity. NBC’s reporting documents cancellations and specific impacts, but not the larger total in the original title.

description_short: Democrats on the House Oversight Committee releases photos from Jeffrey Epstein estate

title: Trump Family Crypto Conflicts Block Bipartisan GENIUS Act
description_short: Trump Family Crypto Conflicts Block Bipartisan GENIUS Act
description_medium: During Senate consideration of the GENIUS Act in June 2025, Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jeff Merkley asked MGX and Binance to preserve and provide records about a $2 billion investment transaction settled using USD1, a stablecoin issued by Trump-linked World Liberty Financial. Their letter raised conflict-of-interest concerns; it documents a request for evidence, not proof that the family’s stake blocked the bill or determined its outcome.
description_long: Throughout spring 2025, the Trump family's financial stake in crypto directly complicated congressional efforts to pass the GENIUS Act — legislation to regulate stablecoins. In April 2025, WLF launched USD1 while Trump was simultaneously pushing the GENIUS Act, creating a scenario where a president would personally profit from legislation he was championing. Democratic senators Warren and Merkley demanded WLF preserve communications between Binance, MGX, the White House, and Trump's sons Eric, Donald Jr., and Barron. Trump's 2025 disclosure showed the family holding 60% of WLF through DT Marks DEFI LLC, with Trump personally taking 75% of net token revenues and holding 22.5 billion $WLFI tokens valued at billions. When Democrats proposed an amendment explicitly banning sitting presidents from profiting from stablecoin products, Republicans blocked it. The GENIUS Act passed the Senate 68-30 on June 11, 2025 without the anti-corruption amendment.

title: Medication Abortion Under Siege: FDA Review, Comstock Threat
description_short: Medication Abortion Under Siege: FDA Review, Comstock Threat
description_medium: A November 6, 2025 Senate letter says FDA Commissioner Marty Makary had committed to a mifepristone safety review and asks HHS and FDA what evidence and process the agencies will use. The senators criticize reliance on a non-peer-reviewed report and request details about expert input and public participation. The letter records their concerns, not FDA findings or a completed review outcome.
description_long: In May 2025, HHS Secretary RFK Jr. directed the FDA to launch a safety review of mifepristone — the first medication in a two-drug regimen used in 63% of U.S. abortions — which experts warned could lead to tighter telehealth restrictions, mandatory in-person prescriptions, or removal from pharmacy shelves. As of July 2025, 12 states had total abortion bans and nine states explicitly banned telehealth-provided medication abortion. The Trump Justice Department was also weighing a broader interpretation of the 1873 Comstock Act that could ban mailing abortion pills nationwide regardless of state law. Texas in September 2025 passed a law allowing private citizens to sue physicians, manufacturers, and distributors from outside the state who mail abortion medication into Texas — a direct attack on blue-state shield laws. Louisiana grand-juried a New York doctor in January 2025 for providing telehealth abortions to a patient in Louisiana.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

title: Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins announced the suspension of federal benefit program
description_short: Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins announced the suspension of federal benefit program funding to Minnesota over alleged fraud allegations
description_medium: On January 9, 2026, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins announced a suspension of federal benefit-program funding to Minnesota, citing alleged fraud. The supplied account does not identify the affected program, the amount at stake or how the suspension would work, and it does not establish that individual recipients lost benefits.
